title: Ephemeral repair agents and step-sequencer for oncall remediation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a lightweight framework to author, register, and execute small, idempotent remediation units ("repair agents") that can be sequenced by an oncall step-sequencer. Repair agents are short-lived, sandboxed processes that perform common corrective actions (eg. drain node, restart replica, bump traffic-weight) with a dry-run mode and strong audit trails. The sequencer composes agents into deterministic flows with conditional branching based on observed signals (health checks, metrics, traces). Goal: reduce mean time to mitigate for Class B incidents by enabling safer, tested remediation steps that engineers can review rather than implement ad-hoc shell scripts during oncall.
acceptance_criteria: Create repair-agent SDK (Go + minimal CLI) for registering an agent with metadata and a dry-run flag
Sequencer service prototype that can run a 3-step flow using registered agents with conditional branching and rollback hooks
Audit log entries persisted for every agent run (actor, args, outcome, stdout/stderr) and viewable in Console (basic table)
Safety constraints enforced: RBAC check, throttle limits, feature-flagged production enablement, and explicit human confirmation for high-risk agents
End-to-end integration test demonstrating recovery for an intentionally injected degraded replica scenario (simulated in staging)
decisions: Execution model: use ephemeral sandboxed containers (gVisor / Firecracker) rather than embedding a generic interpreter in platform processes — chosen for process isolation and easier resource cgroups enforcement
Registration: agents will be declared via a small manifest stored in config-repo and validated on CI; runtime picks from a service registry to fetch latest approved image
Telemetry: emit structured events to ops-telemetry pipeline with standardized schema (agent.name, version, inputs.hash, run_id, duration, outcome)
Authoring UX: provide a minimal CLI + template generator. Avoid a heavy DSL to lower barrier for SREs and engineers
comments: 2026-02-12 — design review: agreed to sandbox agents using gVisor; UX owner assigned to Design for CLI templates (A. Patel)
2026-02-20 — infra spike completed: prototype container launcher + attestations. Found permissioning edge-case when invoking cloud provider APIs; added RBAC gate requirement
2026-02-28 — security review kickoff: requested threat model for agent images, signed image registry requirement; tentative design: dedicated KMS key per environment

2026-03-05 — integration note: connected sequencer to telemetry pipeline. Found that long-running agent output needs chunked log upload to avoid memory spikes — implemented stream buffering in sidecar
2026-03-09 — QA: dry-run mode validated against staging scenario; replayed audit logs to recreate sequence; minor fix to retry/backoff on transient cloud errors
risks: Malicious or buggy agent image could perform unexpected actions — mitigated by signed images + automatic rollback and manual approval for high-risk agents
Overuse of sequenced remediation might bypass deeper root-cause analysis if relied on excessively — include a TTL and mandatory postmortem label for automated runs
Resource exhaustion if many agents run in parallel — enforce global concurrency quota and per-actor throttles
